pr_title: c8d: implement missing image delete logic
pr_body:
<!--

https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

** Make sure all your commits include a signature generated with `git commit -s` **

For additional information on our contributing process, read our contributing
guide https://docs.docker.com/opensource/code/

If this is a bug fix, make sure your description includes "fixes #xxxx", or
"closes #xxxx"

Please provide the following information:
-->

**- Related**
- closes https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/43850
- closes https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/43849
- also related to: https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/45362

**- What I did**

Ports over all the previous image delete logic, such as:
- Implement `prune` and `force` flags
- Implement hard and soft image delete conflics, which represent:
  - image referenced in multiple tags (soft conflict)
  - image being used by a stopped container (soft conflict)
  - image being used by a running container (hard conflict)
- Implement delete logic such as:
  - if deleting by reference, and there are other references to the same image, just
    delete the passed reference
  - if deleting by reference, and there is only 1 reference and the image is being used
    by a running container, throw an error if !force, or delete the reference and create
    a dangling reference otherwise
  - if deleting by imageID, and force is true, remove all tags (otherwise soft conflict)
  - if imageID, check if stopped container is using the image (soft conflict), and
    delete anyway if force
  - if imageID was passed in, check if running container is using the image (hard conflict)
  - if `prune` is true, and the image being deleted has dangling parents, remove them

Also implements logic to get image parents in c8d by comparing shared layers, like what @vvoland did in https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/45265, so that we can prune dangling parents on image delete.

**- How I did it**

With neovim! 👀 

**- How to verify it**

Pull and delete a ton of different images, tag them and use them and try to delete them 😅 
Compare the results, and see if they make sense.

Some examples from me:

issue_context.title: containerd integration: implement "prune" (`--no-prune`) option for image delete
issue_context.body:
### Description

- relates to https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/43820

The containerd implementation does not yet implement the `prune` option

Existing implementation can be found in https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/7624f8aeb1836cd75a0912d9614930e8a59eaf4e/daemon/images/image_delete.go#L295


We should look if this option still makes sense, or if we should deprecate it; it looks now to (mostly) the classic builder, which has a concept of "parent" images (before docker 1.10, all images had "parent" images, but that's no longer the case).
comments: Closing/moving to done since this was fixed by https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/45427

cc @thaJeztah

cc @thaJeztah
Not a blocker, because this is something we need to look at in a wider scope; this would return a containerd error; we may have to translate those to one of our `errdefs` definitions.

Remind me; I was looking into some of these conversions; we have some very silly code-paths where we convert "friendly" name to "fully-qualified" and back (and normalise _again_).

We _could_ consider defining `refString` once, as most "happy" code-paths need it (only in case of an error we discard it);

```go
refString := reference.FamiliarString(reference.TagNameOnly(parsedRef))
```
Looks like `used` is not used anywhere in the containerd implementation.

The user requested pruning, so it feels wrong to me to proceed with the deletion without pruning if something unexpected happens. At this point nothing has been deleted so returning the error here would not subvert the atomicity of the delete operation.

"the user requested" here doesn't really capture the full scenario, as this is default for anyone calling `docker rmi` from the CLI. 
Other than that, yes we can and I might have implemented this differently were this new behavior, but my impetus here was mainly to, as close to 1:1, mimic the behaviour of the non-containerd store image delete, which is to prune quietly and not throw errors in this case. I'd prefer keep this PR as a "port behavior 1:1" and then discuss/propose improvements/changes in a separate discussion.
SGTM

Is there any guarantee that the existence of a dangling image reference implies that there are no other references to the same content? If not, it would be non-deterministic whether the dangling reference to the highest-affinity parent image with both flavours of reference gets deleted. Pruning dangling parents could be made deterministic by modifying `sortParentsByAffinity` to take dangling-ness into account when the images being compared have an otherwise equal affinity.

If there's ever both a dangling reference and another reference, we (the daemon) messed up somewhere. However, there's no "hard" constraint for this, and we don't lose anything by checking that when sorting if we do happen to have a collision, so adding that seems reasonable.

Should one of these be the image name? https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/3f7fde76c2e4e7c234e85c9a8634e2d7639f4f6d/daemon/containerd/image_events.go#L10C1-L11

```suggestion
		i.LogImageEvent(imgID.String(), img.Name, "untag")
```

(or the familiar string from below)?


edit: ❓ looks like the non-containerd implementation does the same, so no need to change (but we should look "why")

Yeah! I wondered the same (but did this over a while so I forgot to call it out when opening the PR) but yes, I left it like this since this was the non-containerd implementation as well. I'll leave it for a follow up to change both/discuss any potential impacts of doing so.
Looks like `used` is not used anywhere in the containerd implementation.
The `prune` argument is unused. Should it be used or should it be dropped?
